screenshots.name: signin-desktop
screenshots.state: Sign-in screen before any details are entered.
screenshots.caption: Sign in with the email address and password your manager set up for you.

screenshots.name: signin-phone
screenshots.state: Sign-in screen on a phone.
screenshots.caption: Atlas works in the phone browser too — the same account signs in on every device.

screenshots.name: signin-invitation-setup
screenshots.state: The Set up your Atlas login page opened from a setup link, with the new password typed twice.
screenshots.caption: A setup link opens Set up your Atlas login: choose a password of at least 10 characters, then Create login.

screenshots.name: home-admin
screenshots.state: Home for the owner 20 minutes before opening: Needs attention, Today’s briefing and Tonight.
screenshots.caption: Home puts what needs doing before service first, with a plain-language briefing of the day underneath.

screenshots.name: home-timeline-glance
screenshots.state: Home scrolled to the briefing, the day’s timeline and the at-a-glance tiles.
screenshots.caption: Scroll down for the day’s timeline and quick counts for stock, recipes and purchasing.

screenshots.name: home-admin-phone
screenshots.state: Home on a phone for the owner, with the tab bar at the bottom.
screenshots.caption: On a phone, Home keeps the same order: what needs attention first, then the briefing.

screenshots.name: home-bartender-phone
screenshots.state: Home on a phone for a bartender.
screenshots.caption: Bartenders see the tasks that are theirs to do tonight — costs and approvals stay with managers.

screenshots.name: shell-sidebar
screenshots.state: The sidebar: Home, Atlas AI, Messages, then the Venue, People and Business groups.
screenshots.caption: The sidebar groups every part of Atlas by what it is for. The badge shows unread messages.

screenshots.name: shell-notifications
screenshots.state: Notifications panel open over Home.
screenshots.caption: The bell collects what changed and what needs you, each with a button that takes you straight there.

screenshots.name: shell-palette
screenshots.state: Search or ask Atlas open with the query “campari”.
screenshots.caption: Press Ctrl K (⌘K on a Mac) and type: items, recipes, orders, people and actions appear as you type.

screenshots.name: shell-account-menu
screenshots.state: Account menu open from the sidebar.
screenshots.caption: Your account menu holds your preferences and Sign out.

screenshots.name: phone-more-admin
screenshots.state: Phone More sheet for an administrator.
screenshots.caption: On a phone, the tab bar holds the everyday pages; More opens everything else.

screenshots.name: phone-more-bartender
screenshots.state: Phone More sheet for a bartender — fewer pages than for a manager.
screenshots.caption: A bartender’s More sheet only lists the pages their role can use.

screenshots.name: ai-empty
screenshots.state: A new Atlas AI conversation with suggested prompts and the conversation list.
screenshots.caption: Start with a suggestion or type your own question. Earlier conversations stay in the list on the left.

screenshots.name: ai-empty-phone
screenshots.state: A new Atlas AI conversation on a phone.
screenshots.caption: On a phone, Atlas AI sits in the middle of the tab bar — tap it, then type, talk or add a photo.

screenshots.name: ai-conversation
screenshots.state: A conversation: the question, Atlas’s answer with the records it used, and a proposal waiting for approval.
screenshots.caption: Every answer shows where it came from — tap a record to open it in Atlas.

screenshots.name: ai-approval-card
screenshots.state: Close-up of a proposal card: a draft purchase order for Northwind with what will and will not change.
screenshots.caption: Atlas never acts on its own. It prepares the change, tells you exactly what will happen, and waits for you to approve.

screenshots.name: ai-decisions
screenshots.state: The Decisions list with open recommendations and past decisions.
screenshots.caption: Decisions keeps Atlas’s open recommendations and a record of what was approved or dismissed, and by whom.

screenshots.name: ai-attachment
screenshots.state: A delivery-note photo attached in the composer, with photo prompts offered.
screenshots.caption: Add a photo — a delivery note, a shelf, an invoice — and ask about it. Atlas suggests questions that fit.

screenshots.name: ai-voice-note
screenshots.state: Recording a voice note in the composer.
screenshots.caption: Hold a thought with a voice note: Atlas writes it out so you can check it before sending.

screenshots.name: ai-live-voice-intro
screenshots.state: The first-time explanation shown before live voice starts.
screenshots.caption: Before live voice starts, Atlas explains that it listens only while the panel is open and that anything it prepares waits for your approval.

screenshots.name: ai-live-voice
screenshots.state: Live voice conversation in progress, with the transcript shown.
screenshots.caption: Talk to Atlas hands-free while you count. The transcript stays on screen, and Mute or End are one tap away.

screenshots.name: messages-channel
screenshots.state: The General channel: channel list with unread badges, named senders with photos or initials, a linked item and read receipts.
screenshots.caption: Messages keeps the team in one place. Each message shows who sent it, and a line marks where new messages start.

screenshots.name: messages-list-phone
screenshots.state: Channel list on a phone with unread counts.
screenshots.caption: On a phone, Messages opens on the channel list; a blue badge counts what you have not read.

screenshots.name: messages-thread-phone
screenshots.state: The General thread on a phone.
screenshots.caption: A thread on a phone: your own messages sit on the right, everyone else’s on the left with their name.

screenshots.name: messages-announcements
screenshots.state: The Announcements channel with an Atlas notice and a manager announcement.
screenshots.caption: Announcements are for official notices. Only managers can post here; Atlas adds notices such as newly published required reading.

screenshots.name: messages-read-receipts
screenshots.state: Close-up of an own message with a linked inventory item and its read receipt.
screenshots.caption: Link a record to a message so the team can open it in one tap. “Read by” shows how many have seen it.

screenshots.name: messages-handover
screenshots.state: The Write handover sheet opened from the Shift handover channel.
screenshots.caption: At the end of a shift, Write handover posts a short note for the next team in Shift handover.

screenshots.name: operations-today
screenshots.state: Today’s checklists and routines with progress.
screenshots.caption: Operations lists today’s checklists and routines with how far each has got.

screenshots.name: operations-checklist-phone
screenshots.state: The opening checklist on a phone.
screenshots.caption: Work through the checklist on your phone — tap an item to tick it off.

screenshots.name: operations-tick-item
screenshots.state: The opening checklist after ticking “Polish and stock service glassware”: now 5 of 9, with your name and the time.
screenshots.caption: Tick an item and Atlas saves it straight away with your name and the time.

screenshots.name: operations-temperature
screenshots.state: Temperature log: one fridge logged, one waiting, and one point without a range set.
screenshots.caption: The temperature log shows which fridges are logged today and flags readings outside the safe range.

screenshots.name: inventory-list
screenshots.state: The Items list with search, Status, Category and Supplier filters; out, almost out and below-par items first.
screenshots.caption: Inventory lists every active item with what is on hand against par. Problems sort to the top.

screenshots.name: inventory-list-phone
screenshots.state: The Items list on a phone.
screenshots.caption: On a phone, each item shows its status and quantity at a glance; tap it for details.

screenshots.name: inventory-filter-menu
screenshots.state: The Status filter menu open on the Items list.
screenshots.caption: Filter by status to see only what is out, almost out or below par.

screenshots.name: inventory-item-detail
screenshots.state: Item details for Campari: on hand, par, supplier, cost, location and recipes that use it.
screenshots.caption: Open an item to see everything about it — stock, supplier, cost and which recipes depend on it.

screenshots.name: inventory-edit-item
screenshots.state: The Edit details form for Campari.
screenshots.caption: Managers edit an item’s name, category, unit, supplier, par level and cost from Edit details.

screenshots.name: inventory-add-item
screenshots.state: The Add item form.
screenshots.caption: Add item creates a new product. Atlas checks for likely duplicates before it is saved.

screenshots.name: inventory-waste
screenshots.state: The Record waste dialog filled in for one bunch of wilted mint.
screenshots.caption: Record waste with a reason — spoilage, breakage or a spill — so stock and reports stay accurate.

screenshots.name: inventory-movements
screenshots.state: The Movements tab: deliveries, waste and adjustments with who recorded them.
screenshots.caption: Movements is the history of every stock change between counts: deliveries in, waste and adjustments out.

screenshots.name: inventory-identify
screenshots.state: Identify item on a phone: the camera recognised Giffard Vanille Syrup with high confidence.
screenshots.caption: Point the camera at a bottle or its barcode and Atlas tells you which item it is. Identifying never changes stock.

screenshots.name: count-start
screenshots.state: The Start stock count sheet: choose an area or the whole bar.
screenshots.caption: Start a count for one area, such as the back bar, or for everything.

screenshots.name: count-counting
screenshots.state: Counting the back bar: 2 of 6 items counted, entering the next quantity.
screenshots.caption: Count item by item. Enter what you see on the shelf; Atlas moves to the next item when you save.

screenshots.name: count-counting-phone
screenshots.state: Counting on a phone, one item at a time.
screenshots.caption: On a phone the count shows one item at a time with a large number field — made for counting at the shelf.

screenshots.name: count-review
screenshots.state: A submitted count waiting for a manager to verify or send back.
screenshots.caption: When the count is submitted, a manager reviews the differences and verifies it — only then does stock update.

screenshots.name: count-list
screenshots.state: The Counts tab with All selected: the back-bar count in progress and earlier verified and cancelled counts.
screenshots.caption: The Counts tab lists every count with its status, who counted and how far it got.

screenshots.name: count-finish
screenshots.state: Finish count for the back bar: four counted, one skipped, one not counted yet, and one big difference.
screenshots.caption: Finish count shows what is counted, skipped and not counted yet, and any big differences to recount before you submit.

screenshots.name: recipes-gallery
screenshots.state: The recipe gallery with availability from current stock.
screenshots.caption: Recipes shows every drink with whether it can be made tonight, based on what is in stock.

screenshots.name: recipes-gallery-phone
screenshots.state: The recipe gallery on a phone.
screenshots.caption: Behind the bar, open Recipes on your phone to check a spec or see what is unavailable.

screenshots.name: recipes-detail
screenshots.state: Recipe detail for the Negroni: ingredients with amounts, cost, margin, glass, garnish and method.
screenshots.caption: Each recipe shows the specification, the cost per serve and the margin at the menu price.

screenshots.name: recipes-edit
screenshots.state: Editing the Negroni: name, category, ingredients linked to stock, price and method.
screenshots.caption: Edit a recipe to change its ingredients, amounts, menu price or method. Ingredients link to inventory items.

screenshots.name: purchasing-orders
screenshots.state: Orders list with one order in each status: Draft, Needs approval, Approved, Ordered, Overdue, Received and Cancelled.
screenshots.caption: Purchasing lists every order with its status, total and expected delivery. Overdue deliveries stand out.

screenshots.name: purchasing-suggested-order
screenshots.state: The Suggested order sheet: below-par items grouped by supplier with an order quantity for each.
screenshots.caption: Review suggestions groups what is below par by supplier. Change quantities, then create the draft orders.

screenshots.name: purchasing-order-draft
screenshots.state: A draft order to Greenleaf, not yet sent for approval.
screenshots.caption: A draft order can still be changed. Submit it when it is ready.

screenshots.name: purchasing-order-approval
screenshots.state: An order to Northwind waiting for manager approval.
screenshots.caption: Orders over the approval limit wait here until a manager approves or rejects them.

screenshots.name: purchasing-receive
screenshots.state: Receiving the Bay Drinks delivery: ginger beer arrived short (12 of 24).
screenshots.caption: Enter what actually arrived. A short delivery keeps the rest of the order open.

screenshots.name: purchasing-order-partial
screenshots.state: A partly received Northwind order: bourbon and two bottles of vodka still to come.
screenshots.caption: A partly received order shows what has arrived and what is still outstanding.

screenshots.name: purchasing-suppliers
screenshots.state: The Suppliers list.
screenshots.caption: Suppliers keeps contact details, items and open orders for each supplier together.

screenshots.name: shifts-week
screenshots.state: The week schedule for 21–27 September with one unpublished change and a change request.
screenshots.caption: The week view shows who works when. Dashed shifts are not published yet; Publish week sends them to the team.

screenshots.name: shifts-bartender-phone
screenshots.state: A bartender’s own week on a phone: Mine view, shifts waiting for confirmation.
screenshots.caption: Staff see their own shifts first, with who they are working with. Shifts marked Needs confirmation are waiting for them.

screenshots.name: shifts-month
screenshots.state: The month view for September.
screenshots.caption: Switch to Month to see the whole month at once.

screenshots.name: shifts-day
screenshots.state: One day opened from the month view.
screenshots.caption: Open a day to see everyone working it, and add a shift from there.

screenshots.name: shifts-add
screenshots.state: Adding a shift for Jón Gunnarsson, 19:00–02:00.
screenshots.caption: Add shift: choose the person, the day and the times. Atlas warns if they said they are not free.

screenshots.name: team-directory
screenshots.state: The team directory with roles, today’s shifts, training and emergency contacts.
screenshots.caption: Team lists everyone with their role, whether they are on today, and what is missing from their profile.

screenshots.name: team-profile
screenshots.state: Gunnar Karlsson’s profile with profile photo, preferred name, contact details and training.
screenshots.caption: A profile holds the person’s photo, preferred name, contact details, emergency contacts and training.

screenshots.name: team-profile-edit
screenshots.state: Editing Gunnar’s profile details.
screenshots.caption: Edit profile sets the name shown in Atlas — the name everyone sees in Messages and Shifts — plus job title and phone.

screenshots.name: team-profile-access
screenshots.state: The Access section of Gunnar’s profile as an administrator sees it: Role, Atlas access, New setup link and Save access.
screenshots.caption: Managers set a person’s role and switch their Atlas access on or off in the Access section of their profile.

screenshots.name: knowledge-library
screenshots.state: The Knowledge library with categories, required reading and a draft.
screenshots.caption: Knowledge holds the venue’s procedures and standards, grouped by category and searchable.

screenshots.name: knowledge-library-phone
screenshots.state: The library on a bartender’s phone with required reading due.
screenshots.caption: Required reading is marked so staff know what to read first.

screenshots.name: knowledge-article
screenshots.state: The “Opening the bar” article, version 3.
screenshots.caption: Articles are easy to read on any screen, with steps, checklists and the version history.

screenshots.name: knowledge-acknowledge
screenshots.state: A bartender reading required article “Cocktail standards” with the acknowledge button.
screenshots.caption: For required reading, staff tap Mark as read when they have read it — managers see who has.

screenshots.name: knowledge-edit
screenshots.state: Editing “Opening the bar” in the article editor.
screenshots.caption: Managers edit an article and publish a new version; staff always see the latest published version.

screenshots.name: reports-overview
screenshots.state: Reports overview for the last 30 days compared with the previous period.
screenshots.caption: The overview puts the month’s key numbers first, then what needs attention and where the money went.

screenshots.name: reports-overview-charts
screenshots.state: Reports overview scrolled to the Money section with spend by supplier.
screenshots.caption: Charts compare suppliers, categories and periods. Sections without a data source say so instead of guessing.

screenshots.name: reports-stock
screenshots.state: The Stock report: value by category and items below par.
screenshots.caption: The Stock report shows stock value by category and which items are below par or not counted.

screenshots.name: reports-date-range
screenshots.state: The period control set to a custom date range.
screenshots.caption: Choose a preset period or your own dates, and what to compare it with.

screenshots.name: marketing-overview
screenshots.state: Marketing overview: coming up, waiting for approval and suggestions; publishing is manual.
screenshots.caption: Marketing plans posts and campaigns. Publishing is done by hand — Atlas reminds you and records what went out.

screenshots.name: marketing-calendar
screenshots.state: The Marketing calendar for September.
screenshots.caption: The calendar shows planned posts by day.

screenshots.name: marketing-editor
screenshots.state: The New post draft editor filled in, with the preview beside it.
screenshots.caption: Write a draft with its caption, channels and planned time, then send it for approval.

screenshots.name: data-imports
screenshots.state: Imports list: a failed invoice PDF, a stock count ready to review and a completed price list.
screenshots.caption: Data › Imports lists every uploaded file and where it is in review. Nothing changes live records until it is reviewed.

screenshots.name: data-import-review
screenshots.state: Import review queue: rows with a possible duplicate and a held supplier row.
screenshots.caption: Import review lists each row that needs a decision, with the issue Atlas found.

screenshots.name: data-import-review-row
screenshots.state: One import row opened: the file’s values beside the matched Campari item, flagged as a possible duplicate.
screenshots.caption: Compare what the file says with the record it matches, then approve, change or reject the row.

screenshots.name: data-issues
screenshots.state: Record issues: missing costs, unlinked suppliers, possible duplicates.
screenshots.caption: Issues gathers gaps in your records — a missing cost, an unlinked supplier, a likely duplicate — with a way to fix each.

screenshots.name: data-pars
screenshots.state: Par levels with suggestions for 7 days of cover, from usage in verified counts.
screenshots.caption: Par levels shows how fast each item is used, based on verified counts, so you can set pars on evidence.

screenshots.name: data-approvals
screenshots.state: Catalogue changes waiting for approval.
screenshots.caption: Changes proposed by staff or Atlas AI — a new item, an alias, a merge — wait here for a manager.

screenshots.name: settings-venue
screenshots.state: Settings › Venue.
screenshots.caption: Venue holds the business details Atlas uses on documents, in Atlas AI and for your team.

screenshots.name: settings-hours
screenshots.state: Settings › Opening hours.
screenshots.caption: Opening hours drive the day in Atlas: when checklists are due, what counts as tonight, and last orders.

screenshots.name: settings-team-access
screenshots.state: Settings › Team access.
screenshots.caption: Team access sets what each role can see and do.

screenshots.name: settings-notifications
screenshots.state: Settings › Notifications.
screenshots.caption: Choose which events notify the team, and turn on notifications for this device.

screenshots.name: settings-ai
screenshots.state: Settings › Atlas AI.
screenshots.caption: Atlas AI settings: switch it on or off for the venue and set daily limits for questions, voice and uploads.

screenshots.name: settings-integrations
screenshots.state: Settings › Integrations.
screenshots.caption: Integrations lists the services Atlas can connect to. Here none is connected yet.

screenshots.name: settings-system
screenshots.state: Settings › System health.
screenshots.caption: System health shows whether Atlas and its data sources are working. Until a check has run, it says so instead of reporting healthy.

screenshots.name: settings-phone
screenshots.state: Settings on a phone: the list of sections.
screenshots.caption: On a phone, Settings opens as a list of sections.

screenshots.name: role-bartender-inventory
screenshots.state: Inventory for a bartender: quantities and status, but no costs or suppliers.
screenshots.caption: Bartenders see stock levels and can count, but not costs or suppliers.

screenshots.name: role-bartender-decisions
screenshots.state: Atlas AI Decisions opened by a bartender.
screenshots.caption: Decisions are for managers; staff see a short explanation instead.

screenshots.name: role-viewer-home
screenshots.state: Home for a viewer (read-only role).
screenshots.caption: The viewer role is read-only: Home shows the same picture of the day, with no purchasing, data or settings.

screenshots.name: role-viewer-inventory
screenshots.state: Inventory for a viewer: read-only, no Add item or Start stock count.
screenshots.caption: For a viewer, Inventory is read-only: no Add item and no stock count.
